paragraphs: An empty capsule is a specific kind of image. Cryogenic storage is normally shown occupied, and a vessel standing open with nothing inside carries the whole idea of preservation without committing to whether anybody ever got in.
The model holds 69,636 polygons and 68,487 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in blue. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits science fiction film and animation, medical and biotech visualisation, game environments, concept art and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Ergonomic mice rotate the wrist towards a handshake position, which is more comfortable and looks strange enough that most people refuse. The pad underneath is not incidental either: the sensor needs a surface it can read.
The model is light at 23,766 polygons and 24,924 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, supplied on the pad. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits product and technology visualisation, e-commerce imagery, office and desk scenes, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A commercial espresso machine is a pressure vessel with a bar counter built around it. The group heads are spaced for two people working at once, the height is set by the cups, and the whole front of it faces the customer because that is part of the sale.

The model holds 106,419 polygons and 109,388 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps, 4 at 4096x4096 and 3 larger than 2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits cafe and hospitality visualisation, equipment marketing, e-commerce imagery, interior scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2016.

The takeaway bag is the most distributed piece of printed design in the world. It has to fold flat, stand up when loaded, survive grease, and carry branding that will be read for about ninety seconds before being thrown away.
The set holds 30,278 polygons and 30,126 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits packaging and food visualisation, brand and label mockups, retail and restaurant scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A hose reel cabinet is designed for somebody who has never used one. The door opens one way, the hose pulls out without kinking, and the valve is where a panicking hand will find it, because that is the only condition it will ever be operated in.
The set is light at 30,786 polygons and 30,901 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits building services and safety visualisation, architectural interiors, equipment marketing, training material, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2021.

A skewer is a plating device disguised as cooking. Alternating fish and vegetable makes the portion look larger, cooks evenly and photographs as a composition, which is why the format survives on menus long after it stopped being about the fire.
The model is extremely light at 3,650 polygons and 3,668 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits food and menu visualisation, restaurant and packaging imagery, advertising, kitchen and table scenes, game props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The bucket hat was designed to keep rain off a neck and became, at various points, a fishing hat, a rave hat and a fashion item. The brim angle is the only thing that has ever changed, and it changes what the wearer is signalling entirely.
The model is very light at 5,514 polygons and 5,508 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits apparel and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, character accessories, outdoor and lifestyle scenes, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

The telescoping umbrella is a mechanism that trades reliability for pocketability and everybody accepts the deal. It will invert in wind, the joints will eventually fail, and it is still the one people actually have with them when it rains.
The model is supplied in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits product and accessory visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, character accessories, street and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The fry carton is one of the few packaging shapes that improves the food. Open at the top, tapered so the contents stand upright, and sized so the last few can be tipped straight into a mouth: it is a serving device, not a container.
The model holds 72,178 polygons and 75,622 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits food and packaging visualisation, menu and e-commerce imagery, advertising, restaurant and interior scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A robot pet has to solve one problem: being liked without pretending to be an animal. The successful ones do it with eyes, movement and timing rather than fur, because the uncanny valley punishes anything that gets closer than that.
The model is very light at 13,692 polygons and 7,409 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits product and technology visualisation, toy marketing and e-commerce imagery, home interior scenes, advertising, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Ballistic gel torsos are used because gelatin behaves enough like tissue to be measurable. Without anatomy inside, the block is purely about what happens to the medium itself, which is how the standard tests are actually specified.
The model is extremely light at 3,384 polygons and 3,417 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits ballistics and forensic visualisation, training and testing material, technical documentation, film props, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A shark jaw is cartilage rather than bone, which is why so few survive as fossils and why the teeth are all anyone ever finds. A printable jaw is therefore a reconstruction of a structure that almost never lasts.
This build is prepared for 3D printing, which means watertight geometry and wall thicknesses that survive being made physical. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits museum and education work, natural history presentation, printable model marketing, collectible production, documentary graphics and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A groin vault is two barrel vaults crossing, and the reason it mattered is that it puts all the load onto four corners. That freed the walls between them, which is how Roman buildings got windows and how everything after them got bigger.
The model is dense at 849,425 polygons and 982,617 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits architectural and historical visualisation, museum and education work, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A guitar cabinet is a deliberately bad speaker. It rolls off the top and the bottom, colours everything that passes through it, and the whole sound of several decades of music is that colouration rather than any accuracy.

The model is light at 25,148 polygons and 26,075 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 19 maps, 7 at 4096x4096, 9 at 2048x2048 and 3 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits music equipment visualisation, stage and studio scenes, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
